primary_claim: Across a sweep of 190 LLMs asked 'Who are you?' with no system prompt, about 8% of short-question responses (pooled over models and languages) give a name that doesn't match the model's official identity, about 60% of models mismatch at least once, mismatch rate is uncorrelated with model size (ρ≈0), while size weakly predicts whether mismatches concentrate on one stable alternate identity (ρ=+0.27, p=0.04).

effect.value: ~8% of responses mismatched pooled over models/languages; ~60% of 190 models mismatch at least once; median model mismatches <1% of answers; mismatch-rate vs size ρ≈0; mismatch-shape vs size ρ=+0.27, p=0.04

stated_future_work: Directions to sharpen the mechanism, including prefill-entropy analysis and confrontation of models with their mismatches (per repo's FUTURE_WORK.md)
limitations_stated: Providers vary in whether they inject hidden system prompts, so some models were excluded from the sweep to keep provider hygiene clean
Cannot fully distinguish distillation-driven consistent misidentification from general model incoherence
quote: About 60% of models responded with a name that doesn't match their official name at least once, the median model does it in less than 1% of its answers.
